memory_update.text: MYRG should be tracked as a smaller public specialty electrical contractor with explicit T&D segment exposure and backlog disclosure; key verification is whether backlog quality and margins improve with grid modernization demand.

PRIM should be tracked as an underfollowed diversified infrastructure contractor with direct power delivery and utility maintenance exposure; isolate Utilities/Power Delivery from broader renewables, pipeline, and civil work.

NVEE is a lower-confidence testing/inspection/commissioning candidate; keep only if filings confirm material utility, power delivery, substation, data-center commissioning, or grid reliability service revenue.

For this node, backlog alone is insufficient: later layers should verify scarce labor availability, safety performance, customer concentration, storm-restoration mix, outage-window scheduling, fixed-price contract risk, and margin stability.

Public pure-plays in relay testing, substation commissioning, drone/robotic line inspection, and utility asset inspection appear scarce; later searches should look for hidden exposure inside engineering roll-ups, geospatial software firms, and small-cap inspection/testing companies.

node: Grid EPC labor, utility field services, testing, inspection, monitoring, and commissioning
summary: Layer 1B expanded the universe around labor-intensive grid execution and reliability services. Quanta Services is the obvious reference anchor, while MYR Group and Primoris are cleaner underfollowed public comps for transmission, distribution, substation, and utility maintenance exposure. NV5 Global is a more indirect but potentially useful testing, inspection, engineering, commissioning, and utility-services candidate for later verification. This pass intentionally avoids electrical equipment mega-cap leaders and focuses on firms that convert grid capex into energized assets through crews, field execution, engineering, testing, inspection, and commissioning capacity.
